acceptance_criteria.criterion: When a repository's clone error contains the credential-missing sentinel text (e.g., "requires a credential for host"), the workspace detail view shows a "Missing Credential" badge instead of a generic error.
The "Missing Credential" badge links to the repository detail view (#/repositories/:id) where the user can select a credential.
Non-credential clone errors continue to display as before (no regression in existing error display).
The credential-missing error detection uses the sentinel text from the error message produced by the orchestrators (WP-007).

summary: Implemented credential-missing error display in the workspace detail view across all four acceptance criteria.
Added CREDENTIAL_MISSING_SENTINEL constant ('requires a credential for host') in workspace-detail.js, matching the sentinel text emitted by the orchestrators (WP-007).

Enhanced runSetup() toast logic: when clone failures contain the sentinel text, the toast specifically mentions 'credential errors' and the affected repository IDs; mixed failures show both sets; pure non-credential failures use the original message unchanged.

Added buildMissingCredentialBadge(repoId) helper: renders an <a class='status-badge status-badge-credential'> element with an amber/orange colour scheme (distinct from the red error badge), linking to #/repositories/:id (URL-encoded) for SPA navigation via _router when available.

Updated buildRepoStatusRow() to accept credentialErrorRepoIds (Set<string>): when statusInfo is null and the repo is in the set, the generic 'No data' badge wrapper is replaced with the Missing Credential badge.
Updated buildStatusTableSection() to forward credentialErrorRepoIds to each row builder.

Added credentialErrorRepoIds Set in renderWorkspaceDetail() closure. Added applySetupResultCredentialErrors(setupResult) helper that: (a) adds credential-error repos to the set and immediately updates their badge cell in the DOM, (b) removes repos that succeeded or had non-credential failures from the set.
Applied applySetupResultCredentialErrors() in all three setup call sites: Setup button (onSetupSuccess), Retry Setup button, and health alert onSetup callback.

Added applyStatusMapUpdate() helper replacing the inline polling loops in doPoll() and doRefresh(): clears credential-error flag and calls updateRepoStatusCells() when a repo transitions from no-data to having status data (i.e. successfully re-cloned).
Added CSS: --badge-credential / --badge-credential-bg custom properties in both light (#c2410c / #ffedd5) and dark (#fb923c / #431407) themes; .status-badge-credential rule with hover state.

Added workspace-detail.credential-error.test.mjs with 9 tests covering all 4 ACs plus toast message variants. All 9 tests pass. All 26 pre-existing workspace-detail tests pass. All 55 other view tests pass. TypeScript compiles cleanly.

comments.note: workspace-detail.js: CREDENTIAL_MISSING_SENTINEL is a module-level string constant. If the orchestrator error message template ever changes, this constant must be updated in sync. A shared constants module (e.g. gui/public/js/utils/constants.js) already exists — consider co-locating this sentinel there alongside STABLE_WS_ID so it is visible to future developers who may not know to look in workspace-detail.js.

workspace-detail.js buildMissingCredentialBadge(): the badge is an <a> element with both href and a click listener for _router navigation. When _router is null (test or direct-link context), the href still works as a fallback. This is consistent with the pattern used in buildHeaderSection's breadcrumb, so no change needed — just confirming the pattern is intentional.

workspace-detail.js: The credentialErrorRepoIds Set is populated only from explicit setup() calls (Setup button, Retry Setup, health onSetup). If the page is loaded when a repo already had a credential error from a prior session (i.e. statusMap has no entry for it from page load), the badge will not appear until the next explicit setup run — it cannot be inferred from the statusMap alone. Surfacing this state on page load would require a new API endpoint or persisting the error in the workspace health report. Out of scope for WP-010 but worth noting for future improvement.

summary: [PASS] Code review completed. All four acceptance criteria are implemented correctly. The implementation is clean, well-documented, and consistent with existing patterns in the codebase. No blocking issues found. No Fix-Forward changes were necessary — code is ready for documentation.

comments.note: Maintainability — CREDENTIAL_MISSING_SENTINEL placement: The constant is declared at module scope with a detailed JSDoc sync warning pointing to both orchestrator files. This is acceptable and fully maintainable. The low-priority suggestion to move it to gui/public/js/utils/constants.js is valid long-term (it would make the cross-cutting contract more discoverable), but the current placement is not a blocking concern. constants.js currently holds only STABLE_WS_ID and APP_NAME_SHORT — both truly global constants. CREDENTIAL_MISSING_SENTINEL is a backend-contract constant; a future shared-constants refactor should include it.

Best Practices — router null-guard pattern: buildMissingCredentialBadge() correctly mirrors the null-guard used in buildHeaderSection's breadcrumb: href provides a fallback for test/non-router contexts, and the click listener is wired only when _router is non-null. Pattern is consistent and intentional. No change required.

Best Practices — runSetup() filter duplication: The credential-vs-non-credential split in runSetup() uses two separate filter() calls over the same 'failures' array. A single reduce() or partition utility would be marginally more efficient, but this is inconsequential at scale (typically < 50 repos). DRY at this granularity would add cognitive overhead without meaningful benefit. Acceptable as-is.

Future Context — Known page-load limitation: When the page is loaded and a repo already had a credential error from a prior session, the badge will not appear until the next explicit setup run because credentialErrorRepoIds is in-memory and not persisted. This is correctly documented in both the implementation and QA pipeline notes, and scoped out of WP-010. A future improvement would persist credential error state in the workspace health report or a dedicated API endpoint. No action required here.

Testing — T2 toast coverage gap (noted by QA): The mixed credential+non-credential toast branch is exercised implicitly via the DOM badge assertions in the AC4 test, but there is no dedicated assertion on the toast text content for the T2 case. All three toast branches (T1, T2, T3) ideally have explicit message assertions. T1 and T3 are explicitly tested. A T2 assertion would complete the toast coverage triangle. Tagged for consideration in a follow-up test sweep — not blocking.
